title: South Korean intelligence estimates North Korea sent more than 12 million shells to Russia
body:
On 13 July 2025, reports based on figures from South Korea's Defense Intelligence Agency (DIA) said North Korea may have supplied Russia with more than 12 million rounds of 152 mm artillery shells. The DIA gave the figures in a report to a lawmaker from the main opposition party, and Yonhap news agency published them. The estimate was calculated by converting shipments into 152 mm single shells.

According to the DIA, about 28,000 containers holding weapons and artillery shells had been sent to Russia so far, along with more than 100 ballistic missiles that were often used in strikes on Ukrainian cities. North Korea had also sent about 13,000 troops since October 2024, mainly to help retake Ukrainian-occupied territory in Russia's Kursk Oblast. CNN reported on 2 July that a further 25,000 to 30,000 North Korean soldiers were being prepared to join Russian forces.

A Reuters and Open Source Centre investigation published on 15 April 2025 found that most artillery shells used by Russian forces in Ukraine in 2024 were made in North Korea. Russia's domestic shell production could not keep up with its rate of fire, which led Moscow to seek supplies from North Korea. Russia and North Korea signed a defence treaty in June 2024, and on 12 July 2025 Kim Jong Un met Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov and pledged unconditional support for Russia's war.
